newsitem.title: USA: U.S. beef producers to increase promotion spending.
newsitem.headline: U.S. beef producers to increase promotion spending.

text.p: U.S. beef producers will raise their spending to promote beef consumption by $2 million this year, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association said.
The Beef Board, which handles promotional spending under the industry's beef checkoff program, will increase its budget by $2 million to $47.5 million in fiscal 1997 (Oct/Sept).
The funds will be used for beef promotion and education among consumers, foodservice operators and health professionals, the NCBA said.
The Beef Board's national spending is in addition to separate local promotional spending of $37 million planned this year by 45 state beef councils, an NCBA spokesman said.
State and local funding for beef promotions is derived from the $1-a-head "checkoff" payment made each time ownership of a bovine animal changes hands in the United States.
The checkoff was mandated under the Beef Promotion and Research Act of 1985.
